title: Special Angles, Trigonometric Equations and 2D Problems
seo_title: Grade 10 Special Angles and Problems Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Derive values of the trigonometric functions for 30°, 45° and 60°; solve simple trigonometric equations for angles between 0° and 90°; solve two-dimensional problems involving right-angled triangles, including angles of elevation and depression.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 10 worksheets: special angles, exact values, simple trigonometric equations, elevation and depression, and 2D problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Make the ratio the subject first.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Learn the special triangles: 30°–60°–90° (sides 1, √3, 2) and 45°–45°–90° (sides 1, 1, √2).
  • sin 30° = cos 60° = ½, tan 45° = 1, sin 60° = cos 30° = √3/2.
  • To solve 2 sin x = 1, first make sin x the subject: sin x = ½, so x = 30°.
  • Elevation is measured up from the horizontal; depression is measured down.

Examples

Example

2 sin² 45° + tan 45°

2 × ½ + 1

Answer: 2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
sin 30° or cos 30°sin 30° = ½; cos 30° = √3/2.
Too earlyMake sin x the subject first.
From the verticalMeasure from the horizontal.

A boat sails 8 km east and then 5 km north. On what bearing must it sail to return directly? (Hint: first find the angle at the end, then use a bearing.)
items.e: tan−1(8 ÷ 5) = 58,0° west of south, so the bearing is 180 + 58 = 238°.

Naledi walks 14 km due north and then 5 km due east. Find the bearing of her finishing point from the start, correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: tan θ = 5 ÷ 14, so θ = 19,7°, measured clockwise from north. The bearing is 019,7° (the distance is 14,9 km).

items.q: A ship sails 13 km on a bearing of 035°. How far north of its starting point is it, correct to 1 decimal place?
